# Results -- Study 238 (Betting-Against-Beta) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly BAB portfolio
(rank by rolling 252-day beta, long leveraged low-beta half, short deleveraged high-beta half,
beta-neutral ex-ante), measured vs SPY on a large-cap S&P 500 survivor panel.
As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 4023 days × 96 tickers | `11f0bf581250` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 4023 days | `482009a8da65` |
| Period covered | 2010-01-04 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 96 large-cap
S&P 500 names (after removing 3 delisted tickers from a 99-name candidate list). The panel
is survivorship-biased -- current S&P 500 members projected backwards.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** only companies that survived to 2026 are in the
sample. Failed firms -- natural short candidates for a quality or low-beta strategy -- have
been removed. All positive results are **upper-bound estimates**.

## The honest test -- BAB portfolio construction

Rolling 252-day beta estimated for each stock vs SPY. Each month, stocks are split at the
median beta. The long leg (low-beta half) is leveraged to unit beta (cap 2.0x); the short
leg (high-beta half) is deleveraged to unit beta. Risk-free rate = 3%/yr constant (no FRED).

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 178 (2011-02 -- 2025-11) |
| Mean return (annualised) | **+4.44%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 13.93%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | +0.319 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+1.386** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 55.6% |
| Max drawdown | -27.1% |

- The BAB portfolio earns **+4.44%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+1.386** -- below the inference bar
  of |*t*| >= 2. The effect is **not** statistically distinguishable from zero at conventional
  significance levels on this 15-year large-cap survivor panel.
- The low-beta leg earns **+13.86%/yr** vs SPY at **+14.08%/yr** -- the long leg barely
  trails the market; the premium comes from the short high-beta leg.
- The high-beta leg earns **+19.88%/yr** unlevered -- after deleveraging to unit beta, it
  becomes a drag (short leg contribution is negative for the BAB portfolio).

## Leverage assumptions

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Leverage cap (long leg) | 2.0x |
| Avg leverage applied | 1.57x |
| Avg deleverage (short) | 0.82x |
| Avg beta (low-beta leg) | 0.641 |
| Avg beta (high-beta leg) | 1.215 |

The leverage cap of 2.0x is a stated assumption. The original Frazzini-Pedersen (2014) paper
assumes unconstrained leverage (borrowing at the risk-free rate). In practice, most investors
face margin constraints, which is precisely the mechanism they propose: constrained investors
crowd into high-beta stocks, inflating their prices and depressing returns. Our 2.0x cap is
a conservative retail/institutional bound.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** HAC *t* = +1.386 (|t| < 2) on 178 months of large-cap survivors.
  The Frazzini-Pedersen (2014) literature provides strong prior support (original paper
  shows robust t-stats on a broad universe), but on this constrained panel the signal does
  not independently clear the inference bar. The positive mean (+4.4%/yr) is consistent
  with the theory but statistically ambiguous. Signal is WEAK rather than NONE because of
  robust academic replication on broader universes.
- **Tradability -- FRAGILE.** Sharpe +0.319, max drawdown -27.1%. The strategy requires
  leverage on the long leg (avg 1.57x) -- a structural cost not modelled here. The 2023
  reversal (-25.9%) shows that the BAB premium can reverse sharply. Leverage amplifies
  both gains and losses.
- **Survivorship -- Named.** The universe is the current S&P 500 projected backwards.
  The true BAB premium on a broad, non-biased universe (including delisted names) is
  likely smaller and harder to trade.
